what: The constructor identifies the depot, customers, visited facts, and location facts from grounded fact names. It parses grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operator names once and obtains their directed metric costs through metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. It also optionally recovers customer demands from numeric effects on the exact load() variable and uses capacity() only when that exact fluent remains available. At evaluation, it reads the current location and unvisited customers, then simulates a capacity-aware nearest-neighbor completion. Each step chooses the cheapest available direct visit or depot-mediated visit, updates simulated load, and finally adds the return-to-depot cost. If complete resource information is unavailable, it retains the routing calculation but ignores capacity. Reusable state, numeric, and routing buffers avoid repeated large allocations.
why: CVRP states are naturally characterized by current location, visited set, and current load, while all routing costs are static. A greedy completion estimate is inexpensive, strongly distinguishes geographically promising successors, and directly reflects the domain's two ways of reaching another customer: continuing the current route or starting a new route through the depot. Reconstructing costs from grounded operators preserves directed costs and avoids unsafe parsing of folded numeric expressions. Optional demand and capacity handling improves estimates on capacity-tight instances, while graceful routing-only fallback remains robust when the translator removes those static fluents.
